narrative.headline: South Gippsland, M≥2 since 26 Sep 2026: 14 events, status unusual.
points: In the South Gippsland box, the window from 26 Sep 2026 to the newest catalogue event has 14 earthquakes of magnitude 2 or more (15 of any magnitude). That count sits at or above the 99th percentile of equal-length windows since 2006. The median historical window of the same length has 0.0 events (95th percentile 2.0).
The last 7 days in that box: 2 events M≥2 (unusual). The last 30 days: 14 (unusual).
Largest catalogue event in the last 30 days of the whole Australian set: M4.9 MLa05 — 8 km NW of Leongatha, VIC at 2026-10-02T16:01:38.438000 UTC.
The ML b-value for this window is 0.51 (n=7, Mc=2.5). Fewer than 50 events sit at or above Mc, so the b-value is too unstable to lean on. The count comparison is the clearer signal.

The public DEA hotspot feed is a rolling window of about 72 hours, not a seasonal archive. This snapshot has 157822 detections, 16732 in the newest 6 hours (2705 distinct H3 resolution-6 cells). 1831 are within 25 km of a Natural Earth place of 10,000 people or more, and 2338 are within 20 km of a medium or large airport. Detections within 25 km of Perth Airport (YPPH): 121.

Geoscience Australia median publication lag over the last 30 days (creation time minus origin, lags under 7 days) is 1 minutes. DEA median processing lag is 36 minutes. These are catalogue timestamps, not a promise about the next alert.
